discussion.title: Reflection on the Sermon
questions: Think back through the sermon and review your notes. What stood out to you, challenged you, or caused you to think differently?

discussion.title: Choosing Joy in Relationships
discussion.intro: Read Philippians 4:1–4. Paul encourages believers to stand firm in the Lord, pursue unity, and rejoice always.
questions: Why do you think relationships and conflict can affect our joy so much?
Are there relationships in your life where conflict, frustration, unforgiveness, or unresolved tension are stealing your joy?
What would it look like to choose humility, unity, forgiveness, and joy in those relationships?

discussion.title: Choosing Prayer Over Worry
questions: What kinds of circumstances or situations are most likely to cause you to worry or become anxious?
Why is it sometimes easier to worry about something than to surrender it to God?
Paul gives us a pattern for prayer: adoration, petition, thanksgiving, and supplication. Which of these comes most naturally to you?
Which one do you need to practice more?

discussion.title: Choosing What Fills Your Mind
questions: How much does what you watch, read, listen to, and spend time thinking about influence your attitude and outlook on life?
What negative thoughts, fears, frustrations, or distractions tend to take up too much space in your mind?
How can you recognize when your thinking is being shaped more by the world around you than by the truth of God's Word?
What would change in your life if you became more intentional about what you allowed to fill your mind?

discussion.title: Choosing Contentment Over Comparison
questions: Why do you think contentment can be so difficult in a culture that constantly encourages us to want more?
In what areas of your life are you most tempted to compare yourself with others?
How does comparison affect your gratitude, relationships, generosity, and joy?
How might practicing gratitude help you overcome comparison?
What is one thing you can thank God for today that you may have been taking for granted?
